decisions.reason: ACE3 was publicly launched as a new industry standard for airfield lighting control and builds on the core business, so heavy investment and public commitment make dropping it unlikely.
The air situation display was promoted to its own page and complements the firm's surveillance and tower offer, so there is little reason to withdraw it despite limited public commitment.
The training program supports the installed base at low cost, and any weak demand can be blamed on temporary pandemic disruption to airport activity.

The lighting training course had little investment and visibility, which makes it easier to drop, but it serves the core airfield lighting business and its weak results can still be explained by the pandemic.
The collaboration software is central to the firm's stated move toward collaborative, data-driven airport operations, so dropping it would contradict that direction.

The MLAT system was announced publicly at inter airport Europe as a flagship, so the high investment and visible commitment strongly favor keeping it, with any shortfall attributed to the temporary collapse in air traffic.
